question: What qualitative laws govern the effect of a difference-of-means activation-steering coefficient on token probabilities, concept presence, and model loss, and how reliably do those laws transfer from an idealized next-token model to real transformers?

key_findings.claim: In the paper's idealized unconstrained-feature model, difference-of-means steering is exactly an exponential tilt of the unsteered next-token distribution by a dataset-derived log-odds score.
key_findings.evidence: Contexts and vocabulary tokens are partitioned into equal, disjoint concepts; every context belongs wholly to one concept; in-concept tokens have probability a_z and all other tokens b_z; and the UFM is assumed to fit those probabilities exactly. Lemmas B.2-B.4 then give steered logits f_alpha(c_j)=f(c_j)+alpha M and probabilities proportional to p(z|c_j) exp(alpha M(z)), with positive M on the target concept and nonpositive M off target.

key_findings.claim: Every nonextremal token has one probability peak as strength varies; off-target peaks precede target peaks, while maximal- and minimal-log-odds tokens are monotone exceptions.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.3 proves a unique bump for z outside the argmax/argmin log-odds sets, orders alpha(j,z_off) below alpha(j,z_target), and makes target argmax tokens strictly increasing and off-target argmin tokens strictly decreasing. Proposition B.1 shows large positive or negative strength concentrates mass on the maximal or minimal log-odds set. The paper's claim that a target bump occurs at positive alpha is only Remark 3.4 for an additional specially parameterized dataset, not part of the general theorem.

key_findings.claim: Target-concept mean token probability is rigorously monotone under the assumptions, but describing the result as a tanh or sigmoidal shape overstates what the theorem controls.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.6 writes the concept change as a shifted tanh of nu_j(alpha), and proves target monotonicity plus conditional off-target decrease or return to the negative baseline change. Appendix B.4 defines nu_j(alpha) as the integral of a strength-dependent conditional log-odds gap; equivalently, it obtains the formula by applying the inverse-logit identity to the concept mass. With no affine or curvature constraint on nu_j, this representation does not determine the number or location of inflection points in alpha. The monotonicity result is substantive; an ordinary sigmoid-in-alpha law is not.

key_findings.claim: Cross-entropy has a nonnegative local quadratic term at zero strength, but the paper's statements that steering necessarily or always degrades performance are stronger than the theorem.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.8 gives Delta CE(alpha)=one-half times the context-weighted sum of Var_j(M(Z)) times alpha squared plus o(alpha squared). The coefficient is nonnegative and can be zero when the log-odds is constant on each context's support; the remainder also does not establish strict degradation for every sufficiently small nonzero alpha in that degenerate case. Moreover, the theorem is local and evaluates the idealized model on its training-context distribution, while pages 6, 9, and Figure A.6 use the stricter language 'necessarily', 'always', and 'inevitably'.

key_findings.claim: Residual-stream steering at extreme magnitude makes normalized transformer logits input-independent and causes loss to plateau, subject to a normalization condition misstated in the proposition.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4.1 states that if each token row v_i is nonzero, then logits converge to LN(plus or minus v) W transpose because the downstream normalized residual update remains bounded. The proof on page 50 says that for LayerNorm the necessary condition is instead P v_i nonzero, where P removes the all-ones direction. A nonzero constant vector has P v_i=0, so the proposition's displayed hypothesis is insufficient for LayerNorm even though it is adequate for the RMSNorm derivation.

key_findings.claim: The real-model next-token plots visually contain the predicted bumps, but their token-selection rule is post-treatment and cannot establish prevalence over the vocabulary.
key_findings.evidence: For each panel, the authors plot tokens selected among the eight highest-probability tokens at alpha=200, or alpha=2000 after normalizing v, explicitly motivated by the large-alpha limit. This conditioning makes the displayed set unusually likely to contain large-alpha winners and nearby bumping tokens. Only Figure A.3 repeats prompt-set sampling (five runs); the main figures omit uncertainty for computational cost, and the paper reports no fraction of all tokens or panels satisfying the theorem's qualitative categories.

key_findings.claim: The appendix materially qualifies the main text's broad sigmoid-validation language: concept curves are only more often right than wrong and are sensitive to concept, layer, model, and judge.
key_findings.evidence: The main text calls the evidence consistent across model types, scales, and concepts and captions Figure 7 as showing the predicted sigmoidal trend. Appendix A.2.2 instead says Theorem 3.6 is only 'partially verified (more often true than false)', early-layer curves are erratic, and Llama 2 is less consistent. Appendix A.2.4 finds the Qwen3-0.6B base judge unreliable and shows Gemma-3-12B falsely counting 'cold' or 'sad' outputs as evil; a revised prompt substantially changes the early spike.

key_findings.claim: The empirical performance audit supports a local U-shaped FineWeb loss and large-magnitude plateau, but provides little evidence for practical task-level degradation laws.
key_findings.evidence: Cross-entropy is plotted on one million processed FineWeb tokens across models, concepts, and layers, without numeric effect summaries or error bars. The only downstream task is Figure A.6: MMLU for one Gemma-3-4B configuration steered toward 'evil', with no uncertainty or concept/model replication. Its curve falls from roughly 60 percent toward the 25 percent random-guess line, but this isolated plot cannot validate inevitability across tasks or separate harmful semantic control from generic capability loss.

key_findings.claim: The paper structures strength search but does not solve strength selection or benchmark its heuristic against adaptive controllers.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion proposes first finding the largest alpha before token collapse or prompt independence and then maximizing concept presence subject to a cross-entropy budget. It explicitly says search is not eliminated and leaves prompt-adaptive rules for future work. Experiments sweep unnormalized, model-specific coefficients and do not compare this two-stage heuristic with LiSeCo, MERA, DSAS, KL-then-steer, prompting, or task-tuned grid-search baselines.

key_findings.claim: The sign-separation engine behind all three UFM laws can fail under the natural extension where both in-concept and off-concept probabilities vary by context.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B.1 states that all main results except Remark 3.4 depend on Lemma B.4. If a_z and b_z are allowed to depend arbitrarily on context j, target-positive/off-target-nonpositive log-odds separation may fail. The authors retain the proofs only by assuming the same separation directly or by a restricted generalization with context-dependent a but context-independent b.

method.core_idea: Reduce difference-of-means activation steering to exponential tilting in a tractable next-token model, derive qualitative strength laws from the induced log-odds ordering, then test the predicted curves over a broad visual sweep of real transformers.
method.mechanism: The theoretical dataset partitions contexts and vocabulary into pure concepts with fixed in-concept and out-of-concept token probabilities. A UFM assigns a free embedding to every distinct context and a linear unembedding, is assumed to reproduce the dataset distribution exactly, and is steered by the mean embedding of positive contexts minus the mean of negative contexts. Multiplying by the unembedding converts the vector into a tokenwise log-odds margin M; softmax then becomes an exponential family in alpha. Derivatives of tilted probabilities yield the unique-bump theorem, a concept-mass logistic ODE yields monotonicity and a tanh-under-reparameterization identity, and the cross-entropy Hessian yields a local variance-weighted quadratic. For practical transformers, the same difference-of-means vector is extracted from 500 generated positive and 500 random or contrastive negative responses, added to the residual stream at all prompt positions, and swept across alpha. Normalization gives the separate extreme-strength input-independence result.
assumptions: The vocabulary is partitioned into equal-size, disjoint concepts, and every context contains tokens from exactly one concept.
For a token z, its probability is the same a_z in every matching-concept context and the same b_z in every nonmatching context, with a_z greater than b_z.
Positive and negative context sets used to form the steering vector have equal cardinality and satisfy the prescribed concept construction.
The unconstrained-feature model perfectly reproduces every empirical next-token distribution; finite-training residuals are ignored.
The theoretical model's free context embedding and linear unembedding are a useful proxy for one residual-stream layer of a transformer.
Mean token probability change over a vocabulary subset is an informative theoretical proxy for sampled, judged concept presence.
Training-distribution cross-entropy in the UFM is an informative proxy for held-out capability and generation quality.
For the large-alpha transformer limit, every steered token row survives the final normalization; for LayerNorm this actually requires a nonzero mean-centered row.
A single global coefficient is meaningful even though steering-vector norms, layers, model widths, and normalizers differ.

techniques.role: Constructs the controlled direction from average residual activations of positive and negative prompt sets.
Makes context embeddings free variables so exact next-token fitting and steering algebra are tractable.
Rewrites the steered softmax as the original distribution reweighted by exp(alpha M(z)).
Uses d p_alpha(z)/d alpha = p_alpha(z) times M(z) minus its tilted expectation to prove unique token peaks.
Aggregates token derivatives into a conditional log-odds-gap ODE for target and off-target concept mass.
Identifies the zero-strength Hessian as a context-weighted variance of the steering log-odds.
Shows that the residual skip term dominates bounded downstream updates and produces prompt-independent limiting logits.
Uses Gemma-3-12B to generate 500 positive and 500 random or contrastive negative responses per concept.
Estimates concept presence from 32 completions at each strength for 12 prompts using a binary LLM judge.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic concept data for an exactly fitted unconstrained-feature model, including a trained example whose cross-entropy reaches about 1.3318 versus dataset entropy about 1.3317.
evaluations.metric: Agreement with exact probability, concept-mass, and cross-entropy formulas.
evaluations.result: The constructed model satisfies the assumptions closely and illustrates unique bumps, ordered peaks, monotone target concept mass, and local quadratic loss.

evaluations.setting: Eleven model configurations: one-layer GPT 0.009B; GPT-2 0.12B, 0.77B, and 1.5B; Gemma 3 1B and 4B; Qwen 3 0.6B, 4B, and 8B; Llama 2 7B; and Mistral 7B.
evaluations.metric: Visual next-token probability-shift trajectories across strengths, concepts, layers, random versus contrastive negatives, normalized vectors, and all-position versus last-token steering.
evaluations.result: Displayed selected tokens often show one bump or monotone domination, with middle/late layers producing more concept-related tokens; early-layer selections are less semantically related.
evaluations.baseline: Theorem 3.3 categories and the large-alpha limit, not alternative steering methods.

evaluations.setting: Twelve concepts: apathetic, depression, evil, humorous, impolite, joy, lying, optimistic, math, coding, medical, and sycophancy; 500 positive and 500 negative generated responses per vector.
evaluations.metric: Tokens selected among the eight highest-probability outcomes at alpha=200, or 2000 for normalized vectors.
evaluations.result: Many displayed tokens are related to the steered concept and show bumps, but selection conditions on the endpoint and no vocabulary-wide match rate is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Random negatives, contrastive negatives, layer/model variants, and token-name annotations in appendix figures.

evaluations.setting: Prompt-set uncertainty ablation for the 'evil' concept at middle layers of three models, resampling P and N five times.
evaluations.metric: Mean and standard deviation of selected-token probability shifts.
evaluations.result: The paper describes variability as moderate and omits error bars from the main figures for cost; this is the only repeated-run uncertainty panel.

evaluations.setting: Concept presence for 12 input prompts and 32 sampled completions at each strength, scored by Gemma-3-12B with a permissive binary prompt.
evaluations.metric: Fraction of completions judged to contain any word linked to the target concept, even if nonsensical.
evaluations.result: Main examples are mostly step-like, but appendix curves are only partially consistent, are erratic at early layers and on Llama 2, and depend on concept difficulty.
evaluations.baseline: Theorem 3.6's mean token-probability quantity, which is not the same metric.

evaluations.setting: Judge robustness on Qwen3-8B outputs at layers 17 and 35 using Qwen3-0.6B-Base, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Gemma-3-12B-IT, and Mistral-7B-Instruct.
evaluations.metric: Shape of the binary concept-presence curve.
evaluations.result: Instruction-tuned judges often agree on step-like curves, whereas Qwen3-0.6B-Base returns unusable all-zero estimates. A separate evil-prompt audit shows false positives for cold/sad text and substantial curve changes after judge-prompt repair.
evaluations.baseline: Four judge models and original versus concept-specific revised judge prompts.

evaluations.setting: Cross-entropy over one million tokens from processed FineWeb across models, 12 concepts, and early/middle/late layers.
evaluations.metric: Delta cross-entropy as a function of alpha.
evaluations.result: Plots are usually locally U-shaped at zero and approach large-magnitude plateaus, with strong asymmetry and model/layer variation; numeric aggregates and uncertainty are absent.
evaluations.baseline: Theorem 3.8's local quadratic and Proposition 4.1's extreme-strength plateau.

evaluations.setting: MMLU under 'evil' steering for one Gemma-3-4B configuration using DeepEval.
evaluations.metric: Multiple-choice accuracy versus alpha, with 25 percent as random guessing.
evaluations.result: The single curve drops from roughly 60 percent near zero toward random accuracy at moderate magnitude, but has no error bars, other concepts, or model replication.
evaluations.baseline: Unsteered accuracy and the random-guess line.

evaluations.setting: Low-data steering with only 10 positive and 10 negative responses over several GPT-2, Qwen, Gemma, and Llama configurations.
evaluations.result: Steering remains visibly effective, but many concept curves oscillate, dip, or collapse depending on layer/model despite captions emphasizing theoretical consistency.

limitations: Author-stated: the theory uses pure, disjoint, equal-size token concepts and contexts containing only one concept; mixed-concept contexts are left for future work.
Author-stated: perfect fitting of the UFM is assumed, removing finite-training and model-misspecification errors.
Author-stated: if both in-concept and off-concept probabilities vary arbitrarily by context, the log-odds sign separation can fail and the main theorems no longer follow.
Author-stated: the theoretical mean token-probability change is different from sampled, judge-based concept presence and the two can disagree when concept tokens remain too unlikely to sample.
Author-stated: concept-curve predictions are only partially verified, with concept sensitivity, early-layer discrepancies, less consistent Llama 2 behavior, and judge-prompt errors.
Author-stated: the work does not eliminate alpha search; prompt-adaptive strength rules and extension to SAE steering remain future work.
Reviewer contradiction audit: Theorem 3.8 gives a nonnegative local quadratic coefficient, not strict global degradation, so 'necessarily', 'always', and 'inevitably' exceed the proved statement.
Reviewer contradiction audit: Proposition 4.1 assumes only nonzero v_i rows, but its proof requires nonzero mean-centered P v_i rows for LayerNorm.
Reviewer inference: Theorem 3.6's tanh formula uses an unconstrained nonlinear reparameterization nu_j(alpha), so it does not prove a conventional sigmoid curve as a function of alpha.

Reviewer inference: next-token plots select the eight highest-probability tokens at the largest positive coefficient, creating post-treatment selection that cannot estimate how common bumps are over tokens.
Reviewer inference: only one five-run prompt-resampling panel reports error bars; model, sampling, and judge uncertainty are otherwise omitted despite dozens of qualitative panels.
Reviewer inference: the concept judge is explicitly permissive enough to accept any related word even in nonsense, conflating lexical mention, coherent trait expression, and degenerate repetition.

Reviewer inference: the theoretical concept metric averages probability per token by dividing by concept size rather than measuring total concept probability; its scale and interpretation depend on the equal-size vocabulary construction.

Reviewer inference: FineWeb is an external corpus rather than the actual training distribution assumed by Theorem 3.8, and cross-entropy is not equivalent to helpfulness, safety, or general capability.
Reviewer inference: practical capability evidence is one MMLU plot for one model and one concept, with no task suite, uncertainty, or comparison to the concept-control benefit.
Reviewer inference: raw alpha is not normalized across the main model sweep, so coefficients and inferred sweet spots are not comparable across model widths, vector norms, or layers.
Reviewer inference: there is no direct benchmark against adaptive-strength methods, task-tuned grid search, prompting, finetuning, SAE steering, or side-effect-reduction methods.
Reviewer inference: many empirical claims are assessed by captions and visual inspection; there are no preregistered curve criteria, panel-level counts, goodness-of-fit values, or hypothesis tests.
failure_modes: A target token can peak at negative rather than positive strength outside the specialized dataset of Remark 3.4, undermining a simple positive-alpha sweet-spot interpretation.
Context-dependent background token probabilities can reverse the target/off-target log-odds separation and invalidate all downstream UFM laws.
If M(z) is constant on a context's support, the quadratic loss coefficient is zero and the claimed strict local performance penalty disappears.
A nonzero LayerNorm steering row parallel to the all-ones vector is annihilated by centering, violating Proposition 4.1's stated sufficient condition.
At large magnitude, output becomes prompt-independent and collapses onto tokens favored by the normalized steering vector rather than coherently expressing the intended concept.
Endpoint-based token selection can make a method appear theorem-conforming even if most vocabulary items or prompts do not exhibit the displayed shape.
Early-layer steering can produce high-probability punctuation, fragments, or tokens unrelated to the intended concept.
A permissive LLM judge can turn cold, sad, decorative darkness, repetition, or gibberish into false positive concept detections.
An instruction-following failure in a base-model judge can yield flat all-zero concept curves irrespective of actual generation behavior.
A single global strength can understeer one prompt and oversteer another because token peak positions are context-dependent even in the theory.
Cross-entropy can improve its visual fit to a U-shape while practical task accuracy, fluency, or semantic control deteriorates at a different scale.
Unnormalized vectors make an alpha range that is safe for one model or layer catastrophic for another.
The proposed two-stage search can optimize a noisy or biased concept judge subject to a loss budget and select lexical degeneration as the apparent sweet spot.
reusable_insights: View additive logit steering as exponential tilting; the derivative of any token probability is governed by its score relative to the current tilted mean.
Separate generic nonextremal bump behavior from monotone extreme-score exceptions when diagnosing steering curves.
Use ordered token peak positions to detect when off-target artifacts begin fading before target tokens stop rising.
Treat a tanh after an arbitrary nonlinear reparameterization as a monotonicity identity, not as evidence of an ordinary sigmoid in the original control parameter.
Express local steering damage through a variance coefficient and report whether it is strictly positive before claiming unavoidable degradation.
For normalized residual architectures, explicitly check whether the steering vector survives centering or RMS normalization before invoking an extreme-strength limit.
Choose diagnostic tokens before sweeping strength, or report vocabulary-wide curve classifications, to avoid endpoint selection bias.
Evaluate concept presence with multiple blinded judges, concept-specific negatives, and coherent semantic rubrics rather than any related word.
Plot control benefit and quality loss on the same Pareto curve and report every coefficient instead of only a visually chosen sweet spot.
Normalize effect size across models and layers, for example by vector norm or induced logit/KL change, before comparing alpha.
Distinguish a theorem's training-distribution loss from external-corpus perplexity and downstream capability.
Audit main-text universality claims against appendix exceptions; here the appendix's 'more often true than false' is the calibrated empirical conclusion.
open_questions: Can the unique-bump and concept-monotonicity laws be extended to mixed-concept contexts without assuming target/off-target sign separation by fiat?
How do finite optimization error and transformer nonlinearities perturb token peak existence, ordering, and uniqueness?
What additional conditions on nu_j(alpha) would prove a genuine sigmoid with controlled inflection and saturation rates in alpha?
When is the variance coefficient in Theorem 3.8 strictly positive, and can it predict held-out utility loss quantitatively?
Can a corrected LayerNorm limit cover steering rows with zero mean-centered component, learned biases, and token-dependent directions?
What fraction of all vocabulary tokens, prompts, concepts, and layers actually match each theoretical curve class under a preregistered classifier?
Can prompt-adaptive alpha be predicted from local logits or peak estimates without sampling a dense coefficient grid?
Do DSAS, MERA, LiSeCo, and the proposed two-stage heuristic trace different control-quality Pareto frontiers under identical vectors and budgets?
Which strength normalization transfers reliably across model families: vector norm, activation standard deviation, induced KL, logit margin, or calibrated concept gain?
Can semantic concept metrics resist lexical repetition and judge contamination while remaining cheap enough for per-prompt strength adaptation?
Does the large-alpha plateau occur before, after, or independently of practical capability collapse across tasks other than MMLU?
How do difference-of-means, SAE, representation-finetuning, and multi-layer steering change the qualitative strength laws?

competitive_landscape.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
competitive_landscape.difference: Turner et al. introduce optimization-free contrastive activation addition and empirically tune signed coefficients for sentiment and detoxification. The present paper analyzes coefficient-dependent probability and loss shapes for a difference-of-means variant, but does not match ActAdd's task-level baseline suite or establish a better selector.

competitive_landscape.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
competitive_landscape.difference: Panickssery et al. average paired positive-minus-negative residual activations and evaluate coefficient-controlled behavior on Llama 2 multiple-choice and open generation, including capability side effects. This paper generalizes qualitative alpha analysis across more models, but uses largely visual curve validation and no direct CAA performance comparison.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. formalize linear representations through counterfactuals, derive steering connections under a causal inner product, and give a partial concept-probability result. The present paper adds token-peak, off-target, local-loss, and extreme-transformer laws, while relying on a narrower pure-concept probability model and explicitly noting disagreement over off-target constancy.

competitive_landscape.title: A Language Model's Guide Through Latent Space
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct empirical strength and side-effect predecessor
competitive_landscape.difference: von Rütte et al. jointly evaluate concept elicitation and fluency, show some concepts require extensive strength tuning or confuse guidance, and empirically report tanh-like concept and quadratic loss trends. The present work provides idealized derivations for related shapes, but its tanh is under nonlinear reparameterization and its empirical quality audit is less task-balanced.

competitive_landscape.title: LiSeCo: Linear Semantic Control for Language Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: The current LiSeCo version uses a closed-form online controller to move activations into a prescribed allowed semantic region with probabilistic/performative guarantees and reports toxicity, sentiment, and language control. The present paper describes global-alpha laws and a search heuristic; it neither enforces a region online nor compares quality-preserving control performance.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:2405.15454v4 (current version checked 2026-08-23; title changed from the workshop citation)

competitive_landscape.title: Steering Without Side Effects: Improving Post-Deployment Control of Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Stickland et al.'s KL-then-steer trains the model to keep steered and unsteered benign behavior close, preventing 44 percent of jailbreak attacks while nearly preserving MT-Bench helpfulness and transferring to TruthfulQA. The present paper explains why large fixed strength causes loss, but offers no learned side-effect mitigation or comparable safety-quality numbers.

competitive_landscape.title: To Steer or Not to Steer? Mechanistic Error Reduction with Abstention for Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Hedström et al.'s MERA jointly optimizes a correction direction and calibrates when and how strongly to intervene, with a provable improve-or-abstain rule and non-degrading empirical correction across datasets and model families. The present paper motivates prompt adaptation from context-dependent peak locations but leaves the rule as future work.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamically Scaled Activation Steering
competitive_landscape.difference: Ferrando et al.'s DSAS v2 computes input- and layer-dependent scaling factors, decouples when from how to steer, and improves the toxicity-utility Pareto front with minimal overhead. The present paper supplies qualitative reasons fixed alpha should be adaptive, but does not implement, tune, or benchmark an adaptive scaler.

competitive_landscape.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. automate natural-language trait-vector extraction, monitor training-induced personality shifts, and use intervention or preventative steering across evil, sycophancy, and hallucination. The present paper reuses similar concepts and generated corpora to study alpha curves, but does not evaluate monitoring, training prediction, or preventative control.

competitive_landscape.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.difference: AxBench directly compares prompting, finetuning, difference-in-means, probes, SAEs, and ReFT-r1, finding prompting best for steering and DiffMean strong for concept detection. The present paper analyzes DiffMean's coefficient but does not place its proposed strength-search heuristic inside AxBench or compare against prompting and finetuning.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first theoretical analysis of activation-steering strength, with precise qualitative laws for next-token probability, concept presence, cross-entropy, and the extreme-strength behavior of normalized transformers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Activation Addition, CAA, Park's representation/steering theory, latent-space guidance curves, LiSeCo, KL-then-steer, MERA, and DSAS all predate or compete with this work. The genuinely distinctive package is the exponential-tilt reduction that unifies token peak ordering, concept monotonicity, a local variance-weighted loss expansion, and an input-independent large-alpha normalization limit, followed by an unusually broad 11-configuration visual survey.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The token-level unique-bump/peak-order result and the local cross-entropy coefficient appear technically nonredundant. The practical novelty is narrower than the headline: ordinary sigmoid shape is not proved because alpha is reparameterized arbitrarily, strict degradation is overstated, the LayerNorm proposition omits a necessary condition, and adaptive-strength competitors already implement the selection behavior this paper leaves as a heuristic.

reviewer_notes: All 50 extracted pages of the current 2602.02712v2 PDF were inspected, including every main result, all experimental figures and captions, the full experimental prompt/judge setup, low-data and robustness panels, negative-strength results, technical lemmas, and complete proofs B.3-B.6. Visual inspection confirmed the post-treatment token selection, the single MMLU panel, irregular early-layer/Llama concept curves, lack of main-panel uncertainty, and the page-50 LayerNorm condition. The extraction is pinned to exact export.arxiv.org bytes. The official arXiv record checked 2026-08-23 identifies v2 (revised 2026-07-08; accepted at ICML 2026). Ten competitors were checked at official versioned sources, including the 2026-renamed LiSeCo v4 and the 2026-07-30 DSAS v2 revision; relationships distinguish earlier theory, direct fixed-strength baselines, adaptive controllers, quality-preserving methods, trait-vector control, and broad steering evaluation.
